source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade DCSCM-CPLD firmware by Redfish when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

original_test_intent: Items and Script indicate a DCSCM-CPLD Redfish upgrade/downgrade with one BMC reset, but the actual Procedure commands an FPGA update. Because these devices have different images, blast radii and recovery paths, the destructive target is unresolved.
original_method: The row PATCHes generic Immediate behavior, POSTs an unspecified image to an assumed update URI and queries generic FirmwareInventory without any component selector. It also exposes a default credential and disables TLS verification.
manual_activity: A platform/library engineer must select the authoritative DCSCM-CPLD or FPGA target and approve the aligned recovery domain. Only after that decision can an authorized engineer approve a destructive API transition; the agent cannot infer the device from DeepSeek, filename or neighboring rows.
required_inputs: explicit engineer decision naming DCSCM-CPLD or FPGA for this code
selected device/board identity and signed upgrade/downgrade images
component-bound Redfish action, selector, task and inventory mapping
secure credentials, trusted TLS, stable power and target-specific independent recovery
safety_requirements: Perform no firmware POST while Items/Script say DCSCM-CPLD and Procedure says FPGA; either guess could write the wrong programmable device.
Do not accept filename or generic FirmwareInventory as a component selector; require a vendor-advertised target binding or signed manifest that is immutable for the transaction.
For a DCSCM decision, ensure recovery and console access do not depend solely on the management module being updated; for FPGA, use its distinct recovery path.
Never execute embedded credentials or `curl -k`, and never retry, reverse or add resets after an uncertain task.
Preserve the Master conflict verbatim and place any correction only in the review/decision overlay.
agent_execution_scope: Before the engineer decision, issue no PATCH, POST or reset and maintain the source conflict plus exact question.
After adjudication, discover and validate a component-specific secure service, bind the image to the selected device and obtain explicit approval before any state change.
Collect target activation, management/host health and recovery evidence without issuing the final verdict.
engineer_actions: Decide whether this row validates DCSCM-CPLD or FPGA and approve aligned Procedure, evidence and recovery in the overlay while preserving the Master text.
Approve the selected image/action/reset/security contract and later assign direction-specific verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek's DCSCM-CPLD assumption matches Items/Script but illegally resolves the conflicting FPGA Procedure. Its generic endpoint/task/inventory flow provides no target proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No write is authorized. After engineering resolves the device, use only a secure vendor component-bound action with response-correlated status and target-specific independent readback.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: DCSCM-CPLD Items/Script, FPGA Procedure, host-off condition, source PATCH/POST/GET, one-BMC-reset criterion and 10/30-minute values remain immutable evidence.

modernized_recommendation.status: ENGINEER DCSCM-CPLD OR FPGA DECISION REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Adjudicate the component, bind a signed image to its exact board/inventory member, use an advertised secure Redfish action, observe the approved single-reset activation and verify selected-target plus platform health through an independent path.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the explicitly selected DCSCM-CPLD or FPGA target.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record selected board/device/image, BMC/Redfish schema, client/CA and recovery-tool revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor update, activation and recovery documentation for the selected component.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an authoritative device decision and deterministic component routing before correcting unsafe transport and task assumptions.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents a successful update to the wrong device from satisfying the row; the non-selected interpretation remains uncovered.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer decision and target-specific vendor contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: DCSCM management loss and FPGA failure require different isolation and recovery procedures.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select versions and tools only after an explicit target decision. It may not silently rewrite DCSCM-CPLD as FPGA or claim equivalent coverage; original and actual targets/methods plus uncovered coverage must be recorded.
expected_evidence: engineer decision naming the authoritative component while preserving both conflicting source fields
selected device/board/version/image matrix with hashes and signatures
advertised component selector/action and redacted correlated completion evidence
target-specific inventory plus affected management/link and host health
independent recovery readiness and engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script name DCSCM-CPLD, while Procedure explicitly says FPGA. The generic POST and FirmwareInventory query provide no component selector, so the hardware destination cannot be inferred safely.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The contradiction concerns the destructive target and recovery domain, not an ordinary missing parameter. Executing either interpretation can program the wrong device, so this row remains BLOCKED until an engineer adjudicates the component.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes PARTIAL to BLOCKED because its DCSCM-CPLD assumption silently rewrites the Procedure and does not prove component routing.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps BLOCKED but refines the basis to the source's explicit device conflict rather than missing project artifacts or unsafe literals alone.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms target ambiguity and adds DCSCM-specific management-recovery consequences and coverage accounting.

review_improvement: Makes the programmable-device contradiction the controlling safety decision and prevents a generic UpdateService transaction from masking wrong-target programming.
independent_technical_reasoning: DCSCM-CPLD and FPGA are not synonyms: their images, inventory members, activation behavior and recovery access differ. With no component selector in the source API example, automation cannot decide which target is intended. This is the narrow V3.1 case where target semantics are irreducibly contradictory until engineering rules on the source.
